title: Band-9 Samples: Do you pay attention to public information about health? [Why/Why not?]
passage_text: This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 12 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 3 Test 1 question: “Do you pay attention to public information about health? [Why/Why not?]” Sample 1: Yes Female Male Absolutely, I take heed of public health advisories. The primary motivation for this is to maintain my well-being. By staying informed about health guidelines and research findings, I can make informed choices about my diet, exercise, and habits. It’s an effortless way to ensure I’m doing all I can to live a healthy life. Sample 2: Yes Female Male Indeed, I do pay attention to public health information. As a member of society, I believe it’s my responsibility to keep myself and others safe. Understanding the latest health advisories helps me to follow appropriate precautions, especially in times of public health crises. It’s more about communal well-being than my personal health. Sample 3: Yes Female Male Definitely, I follow public health updates closely. It’s part of my proactive approach to wellness. Rather than waiting to fall ill and then seeking treatment, I prefer to prevent health issues by adhering to recommended guidelines. It’s more about prevention than cure for me. Sample 4: Yes Female Male Actually, I wasn’t much inclined to follow public health information in the past. But the onset of COVID-19 drastically changed my perspective. The pandemic underscored the vital role of accurate health information in managing such a crisis. Consequently, I’ve become more attentive to public health updates, understanding that they are not just for immediate application, but also for general awareness and preparedness for the future. Sample 5: No Female Male To be honest, I often find myself too caught up in my work to pay close attention to health alerts. It’s not that I’m indifferent to them, but my tight schedule often makes it challenging to keep up with every update. However, I do make time to catch up on major health news during the weekends. Sample 6: No Female Male Regrettably, I tend not to heed public health information. This is largely due to my suspicion of the media and their tendency to sensationalize news, including health advisories, to attract viewership. Consequently, I’ve opted to rely on scholarly articles and studies for my health information. Sample 7: No Female Male Honestly, I’m not one to closely follow public health updates. I have always been in good health and I attribute this to my proactive approach to wellness, which includes regular exercise, a balanced diet, and adequate sleep. This routine has served me well so far, so I see no need to excessively concern myself with every new health trend or study that emerges. Sample 8: No Female Male I must admit, I seldom pay attention to the latest health news or guidelines. My reason? I rely heavily on the traditional healing methods passed down in my family. These long-standing remedies, often made from natural ingredients, have been effective in treating various ailments. I find comfort and effectiveness in these established methods, making the need for contemporary health information somewhat redundant. Sample 9: It Depends Female Male Well, it’s sort of a yes-and-no situation for me. I must admit that I might gloss over minor health notices or tips, as they often seem to be common knowledge or not directly relevant to my lifestyle. However, when it comes to significant health crises like the COVID-19 pandemic, I definitely take note. The impact and scale of such events necessitate my full attention. Sample 10: It Depends Female Male It’s a bit of a mixed bag for me. I do consider public health bulletins, but I place more emphasis on the credibility of the source. With the internet teeming with misinformation, it’s crucial to distinguish between fact and fiction. So, while I don’t disregard public health information, I do sift through it critically.
